tiles: Find style items at any price point using Google Lens
Visual search matches outfits to product catalog
Progressive disclosure UX guides users through looks
challenge: Even though the lookbook isn't filled with products that are being promoted by specific brands, the experience still creates desire. Users see outfits they love but must search for similar items across multiple retailers.
approach: Developed a custom HTML/CSS/JS fashion lookbook that enables users to use Google Lens visual search functionality to identify and purchase any item we style that the price-point best for them without needing to deal with technical tool integrations. The magazine-style layout uses progressive disclosure patterns so users can enjoy the editorial experience first. Built a multi-section architecture handling navigation between different archetypal character journeys and art historical movements while maintaining conversion-focused pathways to product pages.
result: Reduced friction in the inspiration-to-purchase journey by letting users match outfits to products at any price using Google Lens. The UX maintains a magazine experience.
